note: Both sets cover the same core member designations and share the same weaknesses: vague entities ('component', 'framing member', 'member'), heavy duplication of the same section names, and the odd 'W10X | weight | 12 lb/ft' claim that splits the W10X12 designation. Set B adds two claims whose conditions are not supported by the page: 'vertical member' (nowhere stated) and binding HSS4X4X1/4 to detail reference 'S-301 A4' (a detail callout bubble, not a stated member assignment). Set A's extra entries are mostly repeats of facts already captured rather than new errors, so it accumulates fewer wrong claims. Both sets omit the elevation datums (T.O. STEEL 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4", SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0") and several member sizes (L4X4X5/16, C3X6).
remarks: Both sets treat 'W10X12' as an entity 'W10X' with weight 12 lb/ft; the quote 'W10X 12' does not appear on the page as written (page reads 'W10X12'), so this is a shared misread/misbinding. Both miss the key datums T.O. STEEL 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4", SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0", the 1/4"=1'-0" scale, span dimensions (32'-0", 27'-8", 7'-6", 5'-6", etc.), and the L4X4X5/16, C3X6 and repeated PL3"X1/4" members. Neither set binds any section to a specific grid line, column or bay, so most claims are only 'a member of this shape exists somewhere on the sheet' — the elevation labels in the conditions are the only real disambiguators and are applied inconsistently in both sets.
